Can I please have my money back?! 

I went all in with an annual subscription, thinking this was the reputable Renaissance Periodization app. Same brand colors and everything. It’s not. In this app the RP stands for reverse pyramid. I got duped. 

This app is not all bad. I like that it provides video instruction. I like that you can switch the exercise if you don’t have access to the equipment or it’s not feeling good with your joints. 

However I don’t see where it’s tracking my progress. 

(Please know even though my user name is megafart, this is legit.) I wouldn’t recommend this app to even beginners. Can I have my money back?

reviews.title: 25 years + training review
reviews.text:
5/5 for the Right Person, But Not for Everyone**

This app has the potential to be a game-changer for those who are relatively new to hypertrophy or CNS stimulation training. However, it may not resonate with everyone, especially those who have a solid understanding of key principles like periodization, training rep ranges, various advanced techniques such as pre-exhaust sets, partials, intensifier sets, drop sets, strength curves, lengthened/shortened position focus and supersets.

For beginners, this app scratches the surface and provides a structured approach to workouts without overwhelming them with complex concepts. The AI-driven algorithm simplifies the process, which can be beneficial for those who are still learning the ropes. However, for more experienced lifters, this aspect might detract from the art of training such as the freedom to add extra sets or reps, changing exercises that with individual body mechanics. 

Interestingly, I've heard that Nick Walker is using this app, which adds a level of credibility. It could be a helpful tool for him in his journey to bounce back from the previous year. However, when I input my analytics, I found the workout suggestions to lack cohesion, with a disorganized mix of full-body workouts and only two sets per exercise. I was disconnected from the actual workout because I was listening to what a computer said was best for my body instead what my body actually said. This left me unimpressed, leading to a rating of 2/5 for my experience.

In summary, while the app has purpose and merit, it is more suited for novice lifters who are just starting their fitness journey. One thing I’ve learned along the way is, it’s not the workout that’s important as much as it is the execution of that workout. Meaning to say any workout can be amazing if you actually push hard enough, squeeze each rep, feel each rep, train in the pain zone and push yourself to new limits. The only thing holding anyone back from that experience is the individual. You won’t find that in any app. It’s not going to get you or give you any that you have to work for. This is bodybuilding. For those with more experience, it may not align with their training philosophies or needs.
